When reindex is disabled, receiving a 409 (Conflict) or 412 (Precondition Failed)
response means the document already exists in the corpus. This should be treated
as a success case rather than a failure, since the document is already indexed.

This prevents already-indexed documents from being written to failed_urls.txt
when crawlers retry or re-discover URLs that were previously indexed.

subject: Add use_title_for_doc_only config option to DataframeParser (#305)
message:
Add use_title_for_doc_only config option to DataframeParser (#305)

* Add use_title_for_doc_only config option to DataframeParser

Adds a new configuration option `use_title_for_doc_only` that allows
title_column to be used only for setting the document title, without
creating duplicate section titles.

Problem:
When using title_column in element mode, the title appears twice in
the indexed document:
1. As the document title metadata
2. As a section title prepended to the text content

This causes duplicate content and poor user experience.

Solution:
- Add `use_title_for_doc_only` config option (defaults to false)
- When true, title_column is used to set doc_title but not section titles
- Titles list remains None, preventing duplication in document sections

Example config:
```yaml
title_column: title
use_title_for_doc_only: true
text_columns:
  - description
```

With this config:
- Document title: Value from title column
- Document text: Only description (no title duplication)
- Backward compatible: Existing configs unchanged

subject: box: don't infer deletions from incomplete folder listings (#338)
message:
box: don't infer deletions from incomplete folder listings (#338)

* box: don't infer deletions from incomplete folder listings

The incremental Box crawl path uses the result of _get_all_box_files as
the ground truth for "what currently exists in Box" and deletes from
Vectara any file_id in indexed.csv that isn't in that set. When
folder.get(...) or folder.get_items(...) raises (e.g. a Box Shield
Access Policy returns 403), the exception was caught and silently
swallowed, leaving all_files empty. The deletion pass then treated
every previously-indexed document as removed and deleted it from
Vectara — a single failed listing could drain an entire corpus in
one cron run.

_get_all_box_files now returns (files_map, listing_complete). The flag
is set to False if any folder (top-level or recursive subfolder) failed
to list. _crawl_incremental gates the call to _delete_removed_from_vectara
on the flag and logs a clear warning when the delete pass is skipped.
New-file indexing is unaffected — files we positively saw in Box are
still indexed.

subject: gdrive: read shared-drive item ACLs via permissions.list (#346)
message:
gdrive: read shared-drive item ACLs via permissions.list (#346)

* gdrive: read shared-drive item ACLs via permissions.list

Drive's File resource leaves the permissions array empty for items in
shared drives, so file-level grants and grants inherited from
intermediate folders (including group grants) were never seen — files
came back with acl_groups=[] or with groups missing.

Read each shared-drive item's full effective ACL via permissions.list on
the file, which returns direct grants plus those inherited from parent
folders and drive membership. Union it with the cached drive-root
membership (deduped by permission id), kept as a cheap backup. The
ancestor-folder walk is now My-Drive-only.

Verified with probe_acl.py and a before/after ingest: a file with a
file-level grant to a non-drive-member group goes from
acl_groups=['u0c44f21ad9f48092@users.invalid'] on main to
acl_groups=['u0c44f21ad9f48092@users.invalid', 'u3e49dc1aa31bf50d@users.invalid'] with the fix.

* gdrive: document per-file permissions.list ACL reads

The shared-drive ACL path now issues a permissions.list(fileId=<fileId>) per
file (not just the cached drive-root listing), which is what surfaces inherited
intermediate-folder and direct file grants. Update the docs to match:

- config/vectara-gdrive.yaml and crawlers/CRAWLERS.md: describe the per-file
  listing, note ACL resolution is O(shared-drive files) not O(drives) for quota
  sizing, and that a 403 on either the per-file or drive-root listing tags the
  file acl_source: shared_drive_partial.
- shared_drive_admin_access: useDomainAdminAccess applies to the per-file
  listings too, not only the driveId listing.

subject: Fix 12 bugs from full-repo audit: crawler reliability, error handling, credential hygiene (#349)
message:
Fix 12 bugs from full-repo audit: crawler reliability, error handling, credential hygiene (#349)

* slack: fix retry loops to stop duplicate calls and infinite loops

The per-page retry loop never broke on success, so every page of
messages was fetched self.retries times. When all retries failed,
the surrounding 'while True' spun forever, and a failure on a later
page re-appended the previous (stale) page's messages with the same
cursor. get_users_info/get_channels/get_message_replies also returned
implicit None on retry exhaustion, crashing callers.

Introduce _with_retries() that returns on first success and None when
exhausted; callers now abort cleanly with empty results instead of
hanging or crashing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: ub0db06dd1f7d3648 <ub0db06dd1f7d3648@users.invalid>

* mediawiki: fix inverted revisions condition

The check was 'if revisions missing: read revisions[0]', so revision
metadata (last_edit_user/last_edit_time) was never extracted when
revisions existed, and would crash with KeyError when they didn't.

Signed-off-by: ub0db06dd1f7d3648 <ub0db06dd1f7d3648@users.invalid>

* sharepoint: raise on auth-error retry exhaustion instead of returning None

execute_with_retry's 401 branch never raised: a 401 on the last attempt
(or any 401 with auto_refresh_session disabled) fell off the end of the

result-or-exception contract (e.g. the try/except around file listing in
crawl_site), so persistent auth failures — the classic expired client
secret — looked like successful crawls over empty collections instead of
failing loudly. The 401 path also retried with no backoff.

Track the last error and raise it after the loop, and apply the existing
retry delay to auth errors too. Session-refresh behavior is unchanged.
